newsitem.title: UK: British Gas pays up for Centrica demerger.
newsitem.headline: British Gas pays up for Centrica demerger.

text.p: British Gas Plc on Friday revealed that its bill for the planned spinoff of its sales, trading and service business into a new company called Centrica next month would be at least 841 million pounds ($1.42 billion).

British Gas, which after the demerger will rename itself BG plc, said that it would shoulder exceptional charges and provisions of this amount, mainly against its own fourth quarter accounts, in order to pave the way for the split.

The charges come in two large chunks, of which 341 million pounds is to cover the renegotiation of controversial take-or-pay gas supply contracts with energy majors British Petroleum Plc and Mobil North Sea Ltd.

Most such contracts were signed prior to the group's privatisation in 1986 and oblige it to buy fixed amounts of natural gas from North Sea producers at set rates even if it cannot find a viable market.
Such contracts have played a central part in hampering British Gas's recent commercial performance as they have become deeply unprofitable for the group.
The other 500 million pounds of provisions will cover restructuring, including the cost of redundancies, the write downs of surplus property and specific demerger costs.
In this, about 93 million pounds which related to Centrica has been charged to the new company's proforma accounts for the nine months to September 30, 1996 -- its last before it floats.
After taking into account this charge, Centrica made a proforma loss before tax of 452 million pounds in the period, the company said.
This was mainly the result of the absence of one of the year's two winter quarters when the business is most active.
Centrica does not expect to pay dividends in the near future.

The main uncertainty over Centrica's prospects stems from the impending opening up of the domestic household gas market in Britain to competition. This could, in time, erode its key UK base where it has in the past had a monopoly.

Because the split will shift so much of British Gas' sales activities in Centrica, as well as the gas production from its Morecambe Bay offshore field, the new company will use the British Gas brand name in Britain. BG will use it overseas.
The demerger is subject to shareholder apoproval and a vote of shareholders at an extraordinary meeting on February 12.
If it clears the process, the company expects dealings in Centrica shares to start on February 17. ($1=.5922 Pound)
